newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-HINGIS WITHDRAWS FROM GERMAN OPEN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-HINGIS WITHDRAWS FROM GERMAN OPEN.

text.p: World number one Martina Hingis has withdrawn from next week's German Open in Berlin to give herself more time to heal from a knee injury, the WTA Tour announced on Tuesday.

Hingis suffered a slightly torn ligament in her left knee after falling from a horse on April 21 and doctors have recommended the Swiss sensation take another two weeks of rehabilitation, the tour said in a statement.
The 16-year-old Hingis, who has already begun hitting balls, is expected to return to action for the French Open, beginning the week of May 26.

"Though I am disappointed that I am not ready to compete in the German Open, it is better for me to fully recover before returning to the tour," the statement quoted Hingis as saying from her home in Trubbach, Switzerland.
"I feel fine. There is no pain, but I still need a couple more weeks. I am really hoping to be ready for the French."

Hingis became the youngest player ever to assume the number one ranking when she passed Germany's Steffi Graf on March 31. She has won all six singles events she has entered this year including the Australian Open and the Lipton Championships, and has a 1997 singles record of 31-0.
